slides.title: Conditional Independence, Bayesian Networks, and Naive Bayes
slides.visibleText:
DRIVING QUESTION
Which variables still matter once the right evidence is known?

Independence removes factors. Conditional independence removes factors only after a conditioning context is fixed. Graphs make those local claims visible and reusable.

INDEPENDENCE

Test factorization, not intuition alone.

BAYESIAN NETWORK

Encode local conditional distributions in a directed acyclic graph.

INFERENCE

Sum hidden variables and normalize evidence-compatible mass.

NAIVE BAYES

Use a strong class-conditional independence assumption for efficient classification.

slides.title: Independence means learning Y does not change belief about X
slides.visibleText:
THREE EQUIVALENT VIEWS
X ⟂ Y
1
P(x|y)=P(x), when P(y)>0
2
P(y|x)=P(y), when P(x)>0
3
P(x,y)=P(x)P(y), for every x,y pair
INTERPRETATION AND TEST
Observing Y adds no information about X

For a finite joint table, test every cell. One mismatch disproves independence; every match is needed to establish it.

MODELING CAUTION
Exact independence is rare in empirical data. Treat it as a claim to justify or test, not a property inferred from variable names.

slides.title: Factorization replaces one joint table with smaller distributions
slides.visibleText:
DEFINITION
P(X,Y)=P(X)P(Y)
2ⁿ
joint rows for n binary variables
2n
marginal entries if independent
∀
every assignment must satisfy the equality
REPRESENTATION CONSEQUENCE
Store P(X) and P(Y), not every pair

If X and Y are independent, every joint cell is reconstructed from two marginal entries. For n independent binary variables, a 2ⁿ-row joint becomes n two-entry tables.

ASK BEFORE FACTORING
Does the assumption hold for every assignment, and is the resulting approximation accurate enough for the intended decision?

slides.title: A shared cause can explain why two observations move together
slides.visibleText:
FROM ASSOCIATION TO SCREENING OFF
Smoke and an alarm can be associated because both depend on fire

Once the relevant state of the fire is known, a model may assert that smoke contributes no additional information about the alarm. That assertion is conditional—not absolute—independence.

Fire is the common cause; Smoke and Alarm are its effects.

slides.title: Condition on Z, then test factorization inside every Z stratum
slides.visibleText:
EQUIVALENT EQUATIONS
X ⟂ Y | Z
1
P(x,y|z)=P(x|z)P(y|z)
2
P(x|y,z)=P(x|z)
3
P(y|x,z)=P(y|z)
READ THE QUANTIFIER
For all x, y, z with valid denominators

Conditional independence does not say X and Y are unrelated. It says that after Z is fixed, knowing Y does not further change the distribution of X.

WHY IT MATTERS
These local claims are the main representational savings behind Bayesian networks and Naive Bayes.

Cavity can jointly explain Toothache and a probe Catch.
TRANSLATE THE NOTATION
Once Cavity is known, Toothache does not change Catch
P(Catch|Toothache,Cavity)=P(Catch|Cavity)
P(Toothache|Catch,Cavity)=P(Toothache|Cavity)
P(Toothache,Catch|Cavity)=P(Toothache|Cavity)P(Catch|Cavity)
MODEL CLAIM
The equations are equivalent under valid probabilities; whether the claim fits real dental data is empirical.

slides.title: Product and chain rules turn independence claims into factorization
slides.visibleText:
Conditional probability
P(x|y)=P(x,y)/P(y)
Product rule
P(x,y)=P(x|y)P(y)
Chain rule
P(x₁,…,xₙ)=∏ᵢP(xᵢ|x₁,…,xᵢ₋₁)
Independence
P(x,y)=P(x)P(y)
RETRIEVAL CHECK
Use the right rule for the right job
Conditional probability: divide a compatible joint by evidence mass.
Product rule: reconstruct a joint from a conditional and marginal.
Chain rule: factor any joint in an ordered sequence.
Independence: simplify selected chain-rule terms.

slides.title: A Bayesian network is a DAG plus one local conditional distribution per node
slides.visibleText:
REPRESENTATION
Parents identify the variables a node conditions on locally
Burglary
Earthquake
↘    ↙
Alarm
↙      ↘
JohnCalls
MaryCalls

A directed acyclic graph orders dependencies. Each node Xᵢ has a conditional probability table P(Xᵢ|Parents(Xᵢ)).

NODES

Random variables with explicit domains.

DIRECTED EDGES

Direct probabilistic dependencies in the chosen representation.

ACYCLIC

No directed path can return to its starting node.

INTERPRET CAREFULLY
An arrow does not prove causation. A causally designed network needs stronger assumptions than the probabilistic semantics alone.

slides.title: Given the class, treat feature likelihoods as independent factors
slides.visibleText:
FROM CHAIN RULE TO THE SHORTCUT
P(F₁,…,Fₙ|C) ≈ ∏ᵢP(Fᵢ|C)
Class C
apple / not apple
→
size
color
shape

Every feature is conditioned on the same class. The approximation drops dependencies among features within each class.

CORRECT ASSUMPTION
Fᵢ ⟂ Fⱼ | C, not Fᵢ ⟂ Fⱼ

Features such as fruit shape, color, and size may be associated overall because classes occur in different proportions. Naive Bayes asserts independence only after the class is fixed.

CLASSIFICATION SCORE
score(C)=P(C)∏ᵢP(Fᵢ|C). The shared evidence denominator can be omitted when comparing classes.

slides.title: A probabilistic finite-state acceptor models alternative phone paths
slides.visibleText:
Transition probabilities encode alternative phone paths; 0.60 goes directly from /t/ to /m/.
PRESERVE THE MODEL; CORRECT THE LABEL
This is a probabilistic sequence model, not Naive Bayes by itself

A finite-state acceptor assigns probabilities to transitions among phone states. It characterizes pronunciation variants and can help interpret ambiguous phone sequences.

SOURCE NOTE
In the displayed data, 60% of speakers go from the initial /t/ directly to /m/ without an intervening vowel phone.

slides.title: Naive Bayes is efficient, but the variant and dependencies matter
slides.visibleText:
EVALUATION MATRIX
Strength · efficient
Simple counts or distribution estimates; fast prediction.
Strength · incremental
Sufficient statistics can often update from streaming data.
Risk · dependence
Correlated features may count the same evidence repeatedly.
Risk · calibration
Good class accuracy does not guarantee reliable probabilities.
Choose the variant: Gaussian · Multinomial · Bernoulli · Categorical
KEEP, QUALIFY, CORRECT
Efficient: training and prediction are usually simple counts or distribution estimates.
Real or discrete: choose Gaussian, multinomial, Bernoulli, or categorical assumptions appropriately.
Streaming: sufficient statistics can often update incrementally.
Dependency risk: correlated features can double-count evidence and harm calibration.
SPECIFIC CORRECTION
Mean and variance are sufficient only for Gaussian Naive Bayes—not for every Naive Bayes variant.

slides.visibleText:
Assumption
Decision
Parameters
Robustness
CLAIM

Naive Bayes assumes features are marginally independent.

VERDICT

Revise before using this statement as evidence.

CORRECT

No. It assumes features are conditionally independent given the class: P(F₁,…,Fₙ|C)=∏ᵢP(Fᵢ|C).

TEST

Compare held-out accuracy, calibration, error types, and performance under feature dependence or distribution shift.
